subject: Tier pathway consolidation & flexibility questions — pilot to Dedicated conversion
messages:
From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@olivehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: OliveHealth Procurement <procurement@olivehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging inquiry: tier flexibility & seat mixing

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is interested in moving a pilot forward but we have a couple of packaging questions before we put together an internal ask: 

1) Pilot/upgrade/downgrade flexibility: can we start on a short reserved capacity pilot and convert to a Dedicated committed pool later without a full reprocurement? What are the standard windows and proration rules?

2) Feature bundling: we want Advanced Observability + Private control plane for the pilot. Are those add-ons available on the pilot SKU or do they require Enterprise licensing?

3) Seat vs throughput mixing: can we mix a metered host plan + reserved GPU capacity so certain workloads run on the reserved pool while others hit the hosted API? Is there a recommended fallback flow?

4) Pricing / discount guide: for a 6-month pilot with a chance to convert to a 12‑month dedicated contract, what discount tiers do you typically offer for early commit?

If you can send a short summary and sample quote, I can share with procurement. Attaching our procurement checklist for visibility.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Mills
Head of Platform Engineering — OliveHealth
[attachment: procurement_requirements.pdf (pdf)]

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging inquiry: tier flexibility & seat mixing

Jordan — great to hear, and appreciate the checklist. High level answers below; I can follow up with a one-page quote and an example amendment.

Quick summary (pilot → Dedicated path):
- Pilot options: Metered Hosted API (fastest) or Small Reserved Pilot (3–6 month commit on reserved GPUs). Reserved pilot gives predictable performance and KV-cache persistence but requires a short amendment to convert.
- Conversion: We support an amendment to convert Reserved Pilot to Dedicated capacity; standard window is conversion at month 3 or later with pro‑rata credit for remaining reserved months when you upcommit. No reprocurement required if both sides sign the conversion addendum.
- Proration: Charges prorate on a daily basis. If you reduce capacity mid-term, we offer credit toward the remainder of the term (credits do not refund cash). For downgrade to metered, we typically schedule the cutover at the month boundary and issue credits for unused reserved days.
- Add‑ons: Advanced Observability and Private control plane can be included on a pilot, but Private deploys require a minimal security onboarding window (2–4 weeks) and a separate Private addendum. Observability is an add-on SKU that can be trialed for 30 days.
- Mixed routing: Smart routing is supported — you can route by policy (model, latency, region). Recommended pattern: run high‑QPS, predictable paths on Reserved Pilot and leave bursty/spiky traffic on Hosted API. We can set automated fallback to metered variants to avoid errors if reserved capacity is saturated.
- Discounts: Typical pilot -> commit discounts are 10–25% depending on term and commit level. For a 6‑month pilot with intent to convert to a 12‑month Dedicated commit, we usually start the conversation around 12–18% as a baseline.

Next steps: I can draft a short quote that includes a Reserved Pilot (3 months baseline) + Advanced Observability + Private onboarding option, with a 15% starter discount and an amendment path to convert to Dedicated at month 4. If that sounds reasonable, can you confirm target committed GPU hours or an expected token/throughput profile?

Best,
Logan Wright
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0192

From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@olivehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: OliveHealth Procurement <procurement@olivehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging inquiry: tier flexibility & seat mixing

Thanks Logan — that framing helps. A few clarifications from procurement and engineering so the finance team can review: 

- Scope: We expect a pilot that covers 4 production agents at moderate QPS (~150k tokens/day total) and the Advanced Observability bundle. If pilot looks good we want the ability to convert to a 12‑month Dedicated commit covering up to 6 production agents.
- Discount ask: Procurement is pushing for a 20% discount on the committed Dedicated pricing if we convert within the first 6 months. Is that within play?
- Rollback: We need a clear rollback mechanism if latency/regression occurs — ideally a credit for unused committed months or a short term refundable credit.
- SLA: We need an SLA clause for latency targets and an explicit remedy (credit) for breach during pilot and Dedicated phases.

Attaching procurement checklist for legal/controls. Let me know if you need an updated runbook to size GPU hours.

Thanks,
Jordan
[attachment: procurement_requirements.pdf (pdf)]

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Packaging inquiry: tier flexibility & seat mixing — OliveHealth pricing ask

Hi Kimberly / Sean — forwarding Jordan's note. Key points: 6‑month pilot (150k tokens/day), Advanced Observability + Private onboarding option, procurement asking for 20% convert discount if they sign within 6 months and a rollback/credit mechanism.

My recommended approach:
- Offer a Reserved Pilot (3 months minimum) with an option to extend to 6 months. Include Advanced Observability as a trial add‑on for 30 days.
- Conversion discount: approve up to 15% on conversion to a 12‑month Dedicated commit if they convert by month 4. If they convert by month 6, discount steps down to 10%. (Gives commercial flexibility and a clear runway to convert).
- Rollback remedy: provide credit for unused reserved months (applied as account credit) and a one‑time engineering health check. Avoid cash refunds.
- SLA: include standard Redwood latency SLA and a pilot-specific SLA addendum with credit cap (suggest 5% of monthly invoice for serious breaches).

Approvals I need: 
- Kimberly: pricing approval for 15% starter convert discount and credit structure.
- Sean: legal/ops note on Private onboarding time and whether 2–4 weeks timeline is acceptable.

Attachments referenced: procurement_requirements.pdf (from OliveHealth); draft amendment template (I can pull the template if we have approval).

If you OK this, I’ll send a one page quote and a conversion addendum draft to Jordan.

Thanks,
Logan

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Packaging inquiry: tier flexibility & seat mixing — OliveHealth pricing ask

Logan — thanks for the summary. Approve the following with the constraints below: 

- Commercial: approve a 12% conversion discount if OliveHealth converts by month 4. Decline 15% — 12% is our approved threshold for pilot conversion without C-level escalation. If they can commit additional seats or higher throughput we can revisit.
- Rollback: approve account credit for unused reserved months (no cash refunds). Credits must be applied within 90 days and cannot be transferred between legal entities.
- SLA: approve pilot SLA with credit remedy up to 5% monthly invoice for qualified breaches. Legal must sign the pilot addendum.
- Private onboarding: Ops note — 3 week minimum workstream; we cannot guarantee Private deployment in less than 2 weeks. Sean to confirm final timeline.

Logan — please draft the one‑page quote reflecting 12% conversion discount, the credit-based rollback, and attach the standard pilot addendum and legal checklist. Loop Finance for PO/payment terms (we need to confirm invoicing cadence).

Kimberly Park
Director, Commercial Operations — Redwood Inference
